heroHeadline: Egypt Hosts Gaza Phase-Two Talks in El-Alamein; EU Disburses €4 Billion; Heliopolis Tomb Yields Rare Gold Cache
heroSubtitle: Egypt's role as the indispensable Middle East mediator intensified this week as Hamas and Palestinian factions convened in El-Alamein for their third round of ceasefire phase-two negotiations under Egyptian, Qatari, and Turkish mediation — with Foreign Minister Abdelatty coordinating closely with US envoy Witkoff on Gaza and the escalating Iran situation. Simultaneously, the EU finalized its €4 billion macro-financial assistance disbursement (completing the €5 billion MFA package), while the EGX30 stock index held near its 52-week highs at approximately 52,658 points (+62% year-over-year). On the archaeological front, Egyptian antiquities authorities announced the discovery of a rare funeral cache in the ancient Heliopolis necropolis, including gold earrings, inscribed scarabs, and faience vessels from the tomb of an official named Panehsy. Egypt also condemned Iranian attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain, coordinating the Arab response through Gulf diplomatic channels.
footerNote: Data sourced from Egyptian official records, UNESCO, academic Egyptology research (Shaw, Lehner, Hawass), major international outlets, IMF, Human Rights Watch, and institutional analyses.
